claims.text: A dual-framework approach can independently model lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The approach will predict each thermal-conductivity contribution within ±20% of experiment.
The dual-framework approach will outperform earlier single-Debye-temperature estimates.
Earlier methods conflate lattice and electronic heat transport through a single Debye-temperature-based estimate.
The applicable initial state is defect-free, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with controlled stoichiometry.
Approximately 1 wt.% oxygen is consistent with minimal extrinsic defects in the high-temperature samples.
On-the-fly machine-learned force fields can accurately capture HfNbTaTiZr lattice dynamics.
Local lattice distortions alter phonon-scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Effective interatomic force constants from the machine-learned force field quantify the relevant local lattice distortions.
DFT-based electronic-structure calculations can independently assess electron heat transport in this alloy.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions are comparable below 200 K in HfNbTaTiZr.
Concentrated alloys can have substantial and separately relevant lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Lattice disorder and electronic interactions produce distinct scattering processes that should be modeled separately.
Separating phonon and electron transport avoids the oversimplifications of unified Debye-temperature approaches.
The resulting total thermal-conductivity prediction will be closer to experiment than predictions from earlier unified methods.
Existing approaches fail to account separately for lattice distortions and electronic conduction in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The dominant transport mechanism transitions between lattice and electronic contributions at approximately 200–300 K.
Low-temperature calorimetry or frequency-domain thermoreflectance can provide a separated lattice thermal conductivity for this test.
Carrier-dynamics measurements such as terahertz spectroscopy can provide a separated electronic thermal conductivity for this test.

contradictions.description: The samples are described as defect-free or high-purity with minimal extrinsic defects while also being specified to contain approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, an explicit extrinsic impurity.
